major_concerns: Emulator fidelity may not reflect production failure modes (threat to external validity).
Prompt sensitivity and potential prompt-overfitting to the emulator could inflate apparent repair effectiveness.
Single-repair-iteration policy may understate practical repair needs or bias results toward modest improvements.
Details missing on exact emulator, topology selection, and synthetic-apply semantics for the LLM-only baseline.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact emulator(s) (Mininet/version or container images) and include diverse topology classes with justification.
Predefine prompt templates and robustness perturbations; log and report prompt variants and seeds.
Clarify and justify repair-iteration budget; consider reporting results by repair-iteration count (including 0/1/>1).
Define synthetic-apply semantics for baseline (how an LLM-only suggestion is 'applied' for the paired comparison) and ensure parity of observation windows between conditions.

major_concerns: Closed-model APIs may not expose reliable model-native likelihoods or comparable proxies, complicating primary comparisons.
Validator-derived signals depend heavily on emulator fidelity and may be too slow for operator decisioning without latency analysis.
Risk of hybrid-model overfitting to synthetic distribution if train/holdout split not carefully stratified and repeated.
required_design_repairs: Prespecify fallback model-native confidence proxies for closed APIs (e.g., token log-prob surrogates, sampling-based agreement estimates) and document limitations.
Preregister calibration and cross-validation procedures (e.g., repeated random splits or nested CV) to limit overfitting.
Include runtime/latency constraints and report latency-utility trade-offs for execution-derived signals to assess operational actionability.

major_concerns: Privacy and sensitivity of anchored payloads are not addressed (redaction/pseudonymization required).
Using public testnets or third-party timestamping introduces availability and trust assumptions that should be enumerated.
Threat model (adversary privileges, timing, and capabilities) needs clearer definition to interpret detection rates.
required_design_repairs: Specify ledger/timestamping service choice and justify (e.g., public testnet vs trusted timestamping); include availability and cost analysis.
Define payload redaction/pseudonymization procedures and evaluate how redaction affects detectability/reconstruction fidelity.
Operationalize the adversary threat model (exact privileges and actions) and ensure trials cover realistic attacker capabilities; preregister attacker scenarios.

major_concerns: Access, cost, and API constraints may prevent inclusion of representative closed models, threatening comparability.
Prompt-engineering sensitivity may confound inter-model comparisons unless prompts and temperature settings are strictly controlled and reported.
Large estimated model-call budget (4000) may be sensitive to provider rate limits and cost—operational feasibility must be demonstrated.
required_design_repairs: Prespecify exact model candidates including fallback open models if closed models are unavailable; include API/versioning information.
Freeze and publish exact prompt templates, temperature/decoding settings, and retry policy; include prompt-robustness checks.
Provide cost and rate-limit plan (budgeting, throttling, and retry handling) and prespecify how missing model data will be treated in analysis (e.g., exclusion rules).
